content:
tom: Quick check-in on refining the autoscaler <-> operator boundary for dedicated pools. Main ask: avoid double-counting capacity and make burst decisions auditable.

lina: Agreed. Proposal: autoscaler emits an immutable 'scale_intent' with intent_id + requested_gpus + ttl. Operator decides and emits final event.

priya: We also need clear semantics for 'soft' vs 'hard' admits. Soft = ephemeral, can be preempted; hard = pinned until release. Billing and refund differ.

ben: Suggest names: soft_burst, hard_reserve. Soft gets premium multiplier; hard charged against reserve balance.

tom: Good. What about admission ordering when many intents race? Operator should enforce per-tenant fairness and a FIFO within priority buckets.

lina: Implementation: operator keeps short in-memory queue per-tenant and global priority queues. Admission RPC returns admit/queued/deny with reason codes.

priya: Telemetry: operator emits compact events to kafka: event_type, intent_id, tenant, pool, admitted_gpus, node_ids, admit_ts, release_ts, leasing_mode. Billing consumes.

ben: Refund policy sketch: full refund if preempted < grace_seconds (20s), linear decay until 5m, none after. Ledger job computes monetary values offline.

tom: Rollout plan: feature flag feature.autoscale_intents_v2. Start in staging with sim harness, then 10% prod, monitor orphaned_intents and billing_lag.

lina: Add idempotency: operator should accept repeated intent posts; use intent_id as idempotency key and emit final state only once.

ops-bot: Reminder: add sim case `./dev/sim_intents --tenants 200 --burst 60s` to CI matrix. Logs to #eng-runtime in 4h. :robot_face:
